p.seg: Letter on Wrestling a Red Ape
《Letter on Wrestling a Red Ape》
I unexpectedly dreamt of wrestling a red ape,
its strength surpassing that of a pí and hǔ,
for a long time, over and over.
I then observe the heavens,
turn my back to the earth,
and contemplate to the utmost;
it should certainly be without error.
But my lack of understanding,
how can I not be worried?
Auspicious?
Hold me (to the outcome).
Ominous?
Please tell me in detail.
Third month,
Ruǎn Jí informs Yáo Jūn.
Scroll 1
Part 1
"Three Poems of Expressing My Aspirations"
Tiāndì yīnyūn, (Heaven and earth are filled with vital energy,)
yuán jīng dài xù. (The primordial essence succeeds in order.)
Qīngyáng yào líng, (Pure Yang shines brightly,)
héfēng róngyǔ. (And the gentle breeze is leisurely.)
Míngrì yìng tiān, (The bright sun reflects in the sky,)
gānlù bèi yǔ. (Sweet dew covers the universe.)
Wěngyù gāo sōng, (Luxuriant and dense are the tall pines,)
yī nà cháng chǔ. (And graceful are the long shrubs.)
Cǎochóng āimíng, (Grass insects sadly chirp,)
cānggēng zhèn yǔ. (And the oriole shakes its wings.)
Gǎn shí xīng sī, (Moved by the season, thoughts arise,)
qǐ shǒu yán zhù. (I lift my head and stand for a long time.)
Yū hè dì cháo, (How glorious is the imperial court,)
Yī Héng zuò fǔ. (Yī Héng serves as the assistant.)
Cái fēi yǔnwén, (My talent is not for civil administration,)
qì fēi jīngwǔ. (My ability is not for military affairs.)
Shì bǐ Yuán Xiāng, (I will go to the Yuán and Xiāng rivers,)
tuō fēn yúfù. (And entrust myself to the role of a fisherman.)
Yōu zāi! (How leisurely!)
Yóu zāi! (How free!)
Yuán jū yuán chǔ. (There I will reside, there I will live.)
Part 2
Yuè míng xīng xī, (The moon is bright, and the stars are few,)
tiān gāo qì hán. (The sky is high, and the air is cold.)
Guì qí cuì jīng, (Cassia banners and emerald streamers,)
pèi yù míng luán. (Jade pendants tinkle like the mythical *luán* bird.)
Zhuó yīng lǐ quán, (I wash my tassels in the sweet spring,)
bèi fú huì lán. (And wear fragrant orchids as clothing.)

*Yuèlùn* (樂論) [Treatise on Music].
Liú Zǐwèn (劉子問) said:
"Confucius said:
'To pacify superiors and govern the people,
nothing is better than ritual;
to transform customs and change habits,
nothing is better than music.'
Ritual is
that by which men and women are distinguished,
that by which fathers and sons are made,
that by which lords and ministers are established,
and that by which the common people are brought to peace.
Of the tools for governing, none comes before this;
therefore, to pacify superiors and govern the people, nothing is better than ritual.
But the sounds of metal, stone, silk, and bamboo – bells, drums, pipes, and strings;
and the shields, axes, feathers, and yak tails – the deportment of advancing, retreating, bowing, and raising;
what benefit do they have for governance,
and what harm does their absence do to transformation,
that it is said that to transform customs and change habits, nothing is better than music?'"
Ruǎn Xiānshēng (阮先生) said:
"Excellent!
Your question is good.
In the past, Confucius addressed its essence,
but did not elaborate on its details.
Now I will discuss its general principles for you,
and you yourself will provide the details."
"Music is
the embodiment of Heaven and Earth,
and the nature of all things.
When it accords with this embodiment,
and attains this nature,
then there is harmony;
when it departs from this embodiment,
and loses this nature,
then there is discord.
In the past, when the sages created music,
they intended to accord with the nature of Heaven and Earth,
and embody the life of all things.
Therefore, they fixed the sounds of the eight directions of Heaven and Earth,
to welcome the voices of the eight winds of *yīn* and *yáng*,
harmonizing the standard pitch of *huáng zhōng* in a moderate and balanced way,
opening up the emotions and energies of all living things.
Therefore, when the *lǜ lǚ* (pitch pipes) are in accord, the *yīn* and *yáng* are harmonious;
when the sounds are appropriate, all things are in their proper categories;
men and women do not change their places,
rulers and ministers do not overstep their positions,
the four seas share the same view,
and the nine provinces share the same rhythm.
When played on the Round Mound Altar, the heavenly spirits descend;
when played on the square mountain peaks, the earthly spirits respond upwards.
When Heaven and Earth combine their virtues, all things combine their lives;
punishments and rewards are not needed, and the people are naturally at peace."
"The principles of Heaven and Earth are easy and simple,
therefore elegant music is not complicated.
The Way and Virtue are plain and simple,
therefore they are without sound or flavor.
When it is not complicated, the *yīn* and *yáng* naturally communicate.
When it is without flavor, the myriad things naturally find joy.
Day by day, good deeds transform and cultivate without one realizing it.
Customs change and shift, yet are united in this joy.
This is the natural Way,
the origin of music."
"Afterward, sages ceased to arise,
morality and virtue were devastated,
political and legal systems were not established,
intelligence disturbed things,
transformation was abandoned and desires were pursued,
and everyone had their own customs.
Therefore, the teachings of a son are called *fēng* (airs),
and practicing them habitually is called *sú* (customs).
The *fēng* of Chǔ (楚) and Yuè (越) favors bravery,
therefore their *sú* treats death lightly.
The *fēng* of Zhèng (鄭) and Wèi (衛) favors licentiousness,
therefore their *sú* treats wantonness lightly.
Treating death lightly,
therefore there are songs of rushing into fire and plunging into water.
Treating wantonness lightly,
therefore there are melodies of *Sāng Jiān* (桑閒) and *Pú Shàng* (濮上).
Each sings of what they love,
each chants of what they do.
Those who desire it weep,
those who hear it sigh.
Turning their backs and departing,
none are without deep emotion.
Cherishing the pleasures of long days,
embracing the sorrows of long nights,
they gather and unite in it,
they throng and practice it,
endlessly extravagant,
abandoning the bonds of father and son,
relaxing the rules of ruler and subject,
impoverishing the rites of household and family,
abandoning the occupation of farming,
forgetting the joys of a lifetime,
exalting the customs of lewd indulgence.
Therefore, south of the Jiāng Huái, the people are fond of violence;
between the Zhāng and Rǔ rivers, the people are fond of fleeing;
in Wú there is the virtue of the double swords,
in Zhào there are guests who support the qín.
The energy erupts from within,
the sound enters the ears,
hands and feet fly about,
without realizing how shocking it is."
"If people love bravery, they will defy their superiors;
if they are wantonly indulgent, they will abandon their relatives.
To offend superiors results in discord between ruler and subject;
to abandon one's parents results in estrangement between father and son.
When estrangement and opposition contend,
calamity arises and misfortune occurs.
As misfortune occurs, intentions become increasingly divergent;
as calamity arises, concerns become increasingly different.
Therefore, the eight directions have different customs,
the nine provinces have different traditions.
Separated and divided,
they cannot communicate with each other.
Their sounds are different, their atmospheres are distinct,
and their melodies are uneven.
Therefore, the sages established harmonious music,
created peaceful sounds,
established convenient rituals,
and determined compliant appearances,
so that all in the world who made music would follow them as a model.
From the highest to the lowest,
there were degrees of reduction and gradation,
down to the common people,
who all heard of it.
Songs and ballads praised the virtues of the former kings;
bowing and raising the head imitated the deportment of the former kings;
instruments resembled the models of the former kings;
measures and numbers corresponded to the systems of the former kings.
Entering the heart,
permeating the atmosphere,
the heart and atmosphere are harmonious and agreeable,
then customs and manners will be uniform."
"The sage’s movements, whether advancing, retreating, bending down, or looking up,
are intended to humble the body,
subdue the mind,
facilitate what is to be cultivated,
and secure what is to be done.
Songs and ballads
are intended to express harmony and peace,
and to reveal shortcomings.
Bells and drums regulate the ear,
and feathered banners regulate the eye.
Those who listen will not be biased,
and those who watch will not be weakened.
If the ears and eyes are not biased or weakened, then customs and manners will be transformed.
Therefore, nothing is better than music for transforming customs and manners.
Hence, the eight musical instruments have a fundamental essence,
and the five tones have a natural order.
Those that are of the same kind are governed by size.
Because there is a natural order,
they cannot be disordered.
Because they are governed by size,
they can be brought into harmony.
As for the *kōngsāng* (空桑) zither,
the *yúnhé* (雲和) *sè* (瑟),
the *gūzhú* (孤竹) pipe,
and the *sìbīn* (泗濱) chime stones,
their materials are all harmoniously and uniformly tuned.
Sounds should be harmonious,
therefore they must have a fixed location;
using large and small to govern each other,
corresponding to the *huáng zhōng* (黃鍾) *qì* (氣),
therefore they must have a fixed number.
Having a fixed location,
therefore the instruments are precious;
having a fixed number,
therefore their construction is not reckless.
Being precious,
therefore they can be used to serve the spirits;
not being reckless,
therefore they can be used to transform the people.
Their substance embodies the images of Heaven and Earth,
therefore they cannot be made recklessly;
their tones resemble the sounds of distant things,
therefore they cannot be changed recklessly.
The *yǎ* (雅) and *sòng* (頌) have distinctions,
therefore humans and spirits are not mixed;
the rhythmic sections have numbers,
therefore the melodies are not disordered;
the movements have measure,
therefore bowing and raising the head are not confusing;
the songs have a theme,
therefore the words are not contradictory.
Guide them with goodness,
comfort them with harmony,
guard them with sincerity,
maintain them for a long time;
disperse their groups,
compare their writings,
support the young,
aid the old,
causing them to abandon biased customs.
And return to the great transformation of the sagely kings."
"The former kings made music
In order to stabilize the feelings of all things,
And unify the will of the world.
Therefore, they made its sound harmonious,
And its appearance gentle.
Those below do not long for the sounds of those above,
The ruler does not desire the appearance of his subjects,
Those above and below do not contend, and loyalty and righteousness are achieved.
Now, correct music
Is the means by which licentious sounds are warded off.
Therefore, if music is abandoned, then licentious sounds arise.
Hàn Āi Dì did not like music,
And abolished the Music Bureau,
But did not know how to establish correct ritual;
The laws of music were not cultivated,
And licentious sounds consequently arose.
Zhāng Fàng and Chún yú Cháng were arrogant and excessive,
Bǐng Qiáng and Jǐng Wǔ's wealth overflowed the world.
After the abolishment of music,
The lower classes shifted and became even more unbridled.
If the body is not good, lewdness becomes even worse,
rites are not established."
"Punishment and education are a unified body;
rites and music
are external and internal respectively.
If punishment is relaxed, education will not proceed alone;
if rites are abandoned, music will have nothing to stand on.
That there are distinctions between the honored and the lowly,
and grades between those above and below,
is called rites;
that people live in peace,
and their emotions have no sorrow,
is called music.
Carriages, garments, banners, flags, palaces, houses, food, and drink
are the instruments of rites;
bells, chimes, drums, zithers, and song and dance
are the instruments of music.
If rites exceed their regulations, the honored and the lowly will be at odds;
if music loses its order, the close and the distant will be in chaos.
Rites determine its image,
music pacifies its heart;
rites govern its exterior,
music transforms its interior;
when rites and music are correct, the world is at peace."
"In the past, when the people of Wèi 衛 sought elaborate tassels and curved suspensions, Kǒngzǐ 孔子 sighed,
lamenting the decay of rites and the collapse of music.
Now, the bell is the master of sound,
and the suspension is the structure of the bell.
If the bell loses its structure, then the sound loses its master;
if the master and structure are inconsistent, then strange sounds emerge together.
The succession of times of prosperity and decline,
and the changes of ancient and modern times seem as one.
Therefore, when the sage's teachings are abandoned and destroyed, intelligent people all create strange sounds.
Jǐng Wáng delighted in the melodies of large bells,
Píng Wáng favored the tunes of Shī Yán,
high officials and grandees clapped their hands and sighed in admiration,
common people and the masses leapt for joy, eager to hear them.
Thus, proper music was abandoned,
and the music of Zhèng greatly flourished.
The Odes of Yǎ and Sòng were not taught,
but lewd and licentious songs were sought after.
Yán Nián composed the "Tilting City" song,
and Xiào Wǔ thought of the captivating beauty of Mí Màn;
Yōng Mén created the "Pine and Cypress" sound,
and Mǐn Wáng longed for clothes not yet needed for the cold.
Therefore, if seductive and mournful sounds arise,
and sorrowful, resentful, and frivolous lyrics flourish,
then people will later have thoughts of indulging in desires and extravagance,
and people will later have hearts of inward-looking self-indulgence.
Therefore, the gentleman despises the song of Dà Líng,
and hates the dance of Běi Lǐ."
"In the past, the former kings created music,
not to indulge the pleasures of the eyes and ears,
To exalt the intimacy of the secluded chamber,
one must connect with the Qi of Heaven and Earth,
and quiet the spirits of all things.
Firmly establish the positions of high and low,
and settle the truth of nature and destiny.
Therefore, the songs and hymns of the ancestral temple praise the achievements of success,
and the poems of guest banquets extol the principles of propriety and yielding.
The common people are transformed by their goodness,
and foreign customs submit to their virtue.
This is why licentious sounds are regarded as base,
and proper music is esteemed as noble."
"However, ritual changes with circumstances,
and music transforms with the times.
Therefore, the Five Emperors did not share the same systems,
and the Three Kings each created differently.
This is not because they contradicted each other,
but because they responded to changes in the times.
If the common people find peace and comfort in the sounds of licentiousness and chaos,
and destroy the propriety of the former kings,
then later kings must create new music,
each proclaiming their merits and virtues to the world,
adapting and changing it so that the people do not grow weary.
However, they only change the names and titles,
and alter the songs and hymns,
but as for the sound of the music,
it remains harmonious and natural.
Therefore, Huángdì sang of the spirits of Yúnmén,
Shǎo Hào’s songs traced the tracks of the phoenix,
and though the names of "Xián Chí" and "Liù Yīng" were changed,
the pitch of the "Huáng Zhōng" tuning standard remained unaltered.
Therefore, those who understand the transformative power of the Dao can appreciate music,
but those who merely enjoy the sound of music are not qualified to discuss its principles."
"Shùn ordered Kuí to oversee music,
instructing the crown prince in the virtues of moderation and harmony:
'Poetry expresses the intent,
song prolongs the expression,
the sound relies on the song,
and the pitch harmonizes with the sound.
When the eight tones are in harmony,
without disrupting the order,
gods and men are brought into accord.'
He also said:
'I wish to hear the six pitches, the five tones, and the eight instruments,
to regulate them properly,
so as to express the five words correctly.
Listen!'
Excessive hand gestures and licentious music
pollute the mind and ears,
leading to the forgetting of peace and harmony,
which a gentleman does not listen to.
To speak of proper music is to speak of ease, simplicity, and clarity;
with a clear mind and pure breath,
one can understand the musical principles,
and express the five words correctly.
Kuí said:
"Strike and beat the sounding stones,
strum and pat the zithers and lutes to sing,
the ancestral spirits will descend;
the guests from Yú are in their places,
the lords all yield in virtue,
below, the *táogǔ* drums beat,
together they stop and the *zhù* and *yǔ* are used,
the *shēng* and *yōng* bells intersperse,
the birds and beasts prance;
when the *Xiāo Sháo* is performed completely,
the phoenixes will come to dance."
Kuí said:
"When I strike the stone and pat the stone,
all the beasts lead the dance,
the many officials are indeed harmonious."
Poetry expresses intent,
song chants words,
holding the sounding stone and playing the zither,
with sounds that conform to the standard,
recounting the virtue of the former kings,
therefore the spirits of the ancestors descend;
the *shēng* and *yōng* bells are interspersed,
the correct music's sound is faint,
governance is cultivated without harm,
therefore the abundant flourishing prances;
music has measured appropriateness,
completed only in nine movements,
Yīnyáng tiáodá,
and peaceful energies are uniformly circulated,
distant birds come as envoys;
when things are genuine without being overly adorned,
the four seas unite in harmony,
hence the tying of stones and striking of stones,
and the hundred beasts follow the dance.
It speaks of a world of peace and order,
where all things find their proper place,
sounds are not boisterous,
and the signs are subtle and not yet apparent,
hence all officials are in harmony.
Therefore, when Kǒngzǐ heard the Sháo music in Qí,
for three months he did not taste the flavor of meat,
speaking of how supreme music makes people desireless,
their minds peaceful and their qi settled,
not regarding meat as delicious.
From this, we can see
that the sage's music is simply harmony."
"The music of Xīlíng and Qīngyáng all takes from bamboo,
listening to the cries of the phoenix,
honoring the image of the long wind,
collecting from the great forest,
things unseen at the time,
and rarely heard by the common people,
therefore, the world cherishes its virtue and transforms by its spirit.
Thus, when elegant music circulates widely, all things are in harmony;
When the essence is tranquil, listening will not be excessive.
When things are easy and simple, restraint will command the spirits.
When one is quiet and dignified, one will win the hearts of the people:
this was the intention of the former kings in creating music.
From the later periods of decline onwards, the music,
its materials were not genuine,
its instruments were not sturdy,
its standards were not trustworthy,
taking from commonplace things,
being the same as among ordinary people,
each seeking what they liked,
indulging in what their desires dwelled upon,
the sounds of the neighborhoods competed in being high-pitched,
the sounds of the deep alleys strove to be first,
children gathered together to sing of wealth and nobility,
grass cutters and burden carriers sang of lowliness and poverty,
the duties of ruler and subject were not yet abolished,
but one person harbored ten thousand hearts."
"At the end of the Xià Hòu dynasty,
he raised ten thousand women,
clothed them in embroidered garments,
fed them with grain and meat,
they stood and clamored, singing in the morning,
those who heard it were worried and sad,
the world suffered from its disaster,
the people were hurt by its poison.
The last ruler of the Yīn dynasty
They also performed this music,
with pools of wine and forests of meat,
night following day;
yet the sounds of lamentation did not cease,
and enemy states had already seized their zithers and lutes.
Drinking wine in a hall full of people,
weeping as the music played,
were these not all people with sorrows?
Then this music was not truly joyful.
When Wáng Jūchén 王居臣 was in office,
he played new music in the temple,
and those who heard it all choked with grief.
Huán Dì 桓帝 heard the Chǔ 楚 zither,
and was filled with sorrow and heartache,
leaning on his armrest and grieving,
sighing deeply and saying:
"How excellent!
To make a zither like this,
once is enough."
Shùn Dì 順帝, when visiting the Gōng Cemetery 恭陵,
passed by Fán Qú 樊衢,
and hearing the birds singing, was saddened,
tears streaming down his face,
and said:
"How excellent is the birdsong!"
He ordered his attendants to sing it,
and said:
"If the sound of the strings were like this,
Isn't it delightful!"
This is what is meant by taking sorrow as joy.
If one truly takes sorrow as joy,
then what joy is there in the world?
If there is no joy in the world,
and yet there is harmonious balance of *yin* and *yang*,
and disasters do not arise,
that would be difficult indeed.
Music,
makes people's spirits calm and peaceful,
and weakening influences do not enter,
heaven and earth are in harmonious union,
and distant objects come together,
therefore it is called music.
Now, however, one is moved to tears,
sighs and injures the vital energy,
is not suited to cold and heat,
and all things do not flourish.
Even though it comes from string and wind instruments,
it should be called grief.
How can one sigh and lament in this way and call it joy!
In the past, Jì Liúzi faced the wind and played the zither.
Those who listened shed tears, their lapels drenched.
A disciple said:
"Excellent indeed is this zither playing!
It is truly marvelous."
Jì Liúzi said:
"Joy is called goodness,
Sorrow is called grief;
"I am sorrowing,
not for the sake of pleasure."
Judging from these words,
silk and bamboo instruments need not necessarily be for pleasure,
singing and chanting need not necessarily be for goodness,
hence Mòzǐ 墨子 criticizes music.
Alas!
Those who take sorrow as pleasure,
Hú Pī 胡疪 deeply indulged in sorrow without changing,
therefore wished to be a commoner;
Lǐ Sī 李斯 followed sorrow without returning,
therefore his thoughts chased after fleeing rabbits.
Alas!
Shouldn't gentlemen take this as a warning?"

*Dàrén Xiānshēng Zhuàn* (大人先生傳)
Dàrén Xiānshēng (大人先生) was likely an old man.
His surname and given name are unknown.
He described the beginning of Heaven and Earth,
and spoke of the affairs of Shénnóng (神農) and Huángdì (黃帝),
clearly and distinctly.
No one knows the number of years of his life.
He once lived on Mount Sūmén (蘇門山),
therefore the world generally called him *xián* (閒).
Nourishing his nature and prolonging his life,
he shared his radiance with nature.
He viewed what Yáo (堯) and Shùn (舜) busied themselves with as something in the palm of his hand.
He took ten thousand *lǐ* as a single step,
and a thousand years as a single morning.
He traveled without specific destinations and lived without fixed dwelling places,
seeking the Great Dao (大道) and lodging nowhere in particular.
Xiānshēng (先生) used adaptability and harmony,
taking Heaven and Earth as his home.
As fortune declined and power waned,
he remained robustly alone,
He considered himself capable of influencing the workings of nature,
therefore silently explored the Dao and De,
not aligning himself with the world.
Those who valued themselves criticized him, and the ignorant found him strange,
not understanding his transformations and divine subtleties;
yet Xiānshēng did not alter his pursuits because of the world's criticism and strangeness.
Xiānshēng believed that the Central Plains within the world was no more significant than a fly or mosquito on a curtain,
therefore ultimately did not consider it a matter of importance,
and focused his intentions on foreign and extraordinary regions,
traveling and enjoying sights,
unseen by the world,
wandering without end.
He left his writings on Mount Sūmén and departed,
and the world knew not where he went.
Someone, perhaps someone of great importance, wrote a letter to Xiānshēng, saying:
"Among the valued things in the world,
nothing is more valued than a Jūnzǐ:
Their clothing has fixed colors,
their appearance has fixed rules,
their speech has fixed measures,
their conduct has fixed patterns;
When standing, they bow deeply,
with hands clasped as if holding a drum,
their movements and stillness are regulated,
their steps measured like musical notes,
their advances and retreats, their turns and circles,
all have established rules.
If the heart harbors ice,
Trembling and shuddering,
Restraining oneself and cultivating virtue,
Being cautious day by day,
Choosing one's path carefully,
Fearing to leave anything out,
Reciting the teachings of Zhōu (周) and Kǒng (孔),
Admiring the virtues of Táng (唐) and Yú (虞),
Upholding only the law,
Mastering only the rites,
Holding guī (珪) and bì (璧) in hand,
Walking with feet aligned to the plumb line,
Seeking to make one's actions a model for the present,
Seeking to make one's words a standard for eternity;
In youth, praised by the village,
In adulthood, renowned in the state,
Aspiring to attain the position of Sāngōng (三公),
And at the very least, not failing as a governor of one of the Jiǔzhōu (九州),
Therefore, possessing gold and jade,
Adorning oneself with flowing ribbons,
Enjoying a position of honor,
Receiving land as fief,
Spreading one's fame to later generations,
Equaling one's merits to those of the ancients;
Serving the sovereign,
Nurturing the people,
Retreating to manage one's private household,
Raising and nurturing one's wife and children,
Choosing a propitious site for a dwelling,
one anticipates myriad blessings.
Keeping distant from calamity and drawing near to good fortune,
one forever strengthens oneself.
This truly is the noble aspiration of the refined gentleman,
a beautiful conduct that has not changed from ancient times to the present.
Now, you, sir, dwell with dishevelled hair amidst the vast ocean,
far from such gentlemen.
I fear the world will lament you, sir, and criticize you.

"Ten Four-Character Poems by Ruǎn Jí"
The sun's essence blazes brightly,
plants and trees are withered and sparse.
Valley winds fan away the heat,
dense clouds gather heavily.
Flashing lightning shakes the light,
swift thunder leaves its sound.
Drizzling rain descends,
scattering over the northern forest.
A light boat floats gently,
now adrift, now submerged.
Feeling for the past, lamenting the coming,
cherishing antiquity, grieving the present.
Birth and life are determined by fate,
time passes, worries deepen.
How to express my thoughts?
Through whistling and prolonged singing.
Who can uphold their aspirations,
Like jade, like gold.
In sorrow, not wounded;
In joy, not dissolute.
Respectfully receiving your bright teachings,
To comfort my heart.
Established images shine brightly,
Yin and yang pass through.
Autumn winds are swift and harsh,
White dew falls at night.
Tall forests are stripped bare,
Luxuriant grasses lose their splendor.
Good times suddenly pass,
The morning sun inclines westward.
There is a beginning and an end,
Who can remain full for long?
Tài Wēi opens the way,
The three celestial luminaries shed their essence.
The majestic dragons,
Leap and soar in the purple courtyard.
Scales divide, withering away,
Times are high, and the road is clear.
Sometimes hidden, sometimes silent,
Concealing shadows and vanishing forms.
I wish to preserve this day,
To forever match my lengthened years.
The armillary sphere turns swiftly,
The four seasons pass unnoticed.
Winter days are bleak and desolate;
Dark clouds obscure the sky.
Pure ice fills the marshes;
White snow clings to the mountains.
Time swiftly passes,
Like a flowing stream.
Who does not strive,
Valuing a complete reputation?
The great road is smooth and wide;
Side paths are for those who vie for precedence.
Black and yellow are covered in dust;
Red and purple are bright and fresh.
Alas, my revered Kǒng Fù,
Your sagely virtue penetrates the mysterious.
Glory that is not righteous,
Vanishes like dust and smoke.
Though I lack spiritual virtue,
I wish to hide myself in the depths.
Morning clouds gather from all directions,
But disperse at dusk.
The white sun casts its light;
Bright stars shine brilliantly.
Solemnly soar the phoenixes;
Harmoniously call the wild geese.
If I do not enjoy myself now,
The years will be late in passing.
Jiāng Sǒu assisted Zhōu,
Zǐfáng supported the Hàn.
Responding to the appointed time, aiding the mandate,
Meritorious achievements pacifying chaos.
His person employed, his merit evident,
His virtue praised by his name.
The world lacks past events,
His talents are not those of a transient era.
Entrusting fate to [blank],
Accepting Heaven without complaint.
Alas, you noble gentlemen,
Why do you sigh eternally?
The sun and moon shine brightly,
Capable of reflecting the wisdom of Heaven.
Three Empresses attend court,
Twenty-four are promoted to office.
Elevating our talents,
Dismissing those stubborn and wicked.
The highest ideal is to establish virtue,
Next is to establish merit.
Benevolent influence widely bestowed,
Mysterious transformations subtly spread.
Fortunate to encounter a time of great enlightenment,
To witness this era of harmony.
Dwelling in a humble gate,
Following only the dictates of my will.
Entering and retiring take different paths,
Looking up and down, appearances differ.
Gazing and sighing at the deeds of the ancients.
Aspiring to surpass lofty footsteps.
Praising this Jī Shān 箕山,
Neglecting that Yú Lóng 虞龍.
Ascending high and gazing afar,
Surveying the eight corners all around.
Mountains and rivers are distant and vast,
Long roads diverge and differ.
I am moved by Mòzǐ 墨子,
Cherishing Yáng Zhū's 楊朱 thoughts.
Embracing my shadow, standing alone like a crane,
Stretching my neck, hesitating and pacing back and forth.
Looking up at soaring birds,
Looking down at swimming fish.
Red forests are misty with clouds,
Green leaves unfurl in the wind.
Nature's creation is dense and brimming,
All things are abundantly displayed.
What is large is insufficient,
What is simple has more than enough.
How shall I nourish my will?
Guard it with emptiness and tranquility.
I still hope that in a different age,
Ten thousand years from now, we will share the same ideals.
Insignificant are my followers,
Great and orderly are the plans.
Diligently studying classic texts,
my thoughts are immersed and linger.
So I command my servants,
to set out on a journey.
Vast and mighty is the great river,
afloat and wandering is the poplar boat.
Looking up, I gaze at the bright sunlight,
looking down, I observe the flowing waves.
The sun and moon move eastward,
the bright sunlight sets in the west.
Cold departs and heat arrives,
the four seasons alternate in cycles.
Luxuriant blooms in flourishing spring,
dense leaves fall in withered autumn.
Youthful years decline and wane,
suddenly, like floating.
Carefree and leisurely,
without resentment towards the world.
I go to the northern forest,
to wander on the banks of that river.
Looking up, I climb the jade branches,
looking down, I observe the white fishing lines.
A hidden phoenix perches with folded wings,
a submerged dragon leaps with scales.
Secluded light conceals its form,
embodying transformation to respond to the divine.
The noble person advances in virtue,
dwells in simplicity and cherishes purity.
Amassing wealth invites criticism,
a bamboo basket and gourd are praised as benevolent.
Yí Shū pick ferns,
their pure loftiness is renowned far and wide.
Qí Jǐng's thousand chariots,
are like dust to this.
Alas, you later generations,
cultivate this moral principle.
A humble gate and small window,
are said to be the true Way.
Beautiful countenance and alluring beauty,
are uniquely displayed throughout the ages.
Seductive and extraordinarily beautiful,
gentle as the clear brightness.
Black hair and moth eyebrows,
extend and transmit radiance.
Elegant ornaments and beautiful silk,
carried by the wind, leave behind fragrance.
Looking back, one realizes the essence,
the soul is shot forth, flying high.
The noble person controls himself,
his heart is pure as ice and frost.
Dimly, confused and chaotic,
were the two kings of old.
Jade terraces and revolving chambers,
The long night, the golden beams.
The Yin clan overthrew the Xia dynasty,
The Zhou cut down Zhou of Shang.
Alas, later generations,
such cause for sorrow.
The morning wind sweeps away the dust,
the morning rain sprinkles the road.
The swift team of horses flies, dragon-like ascending,
sadly neighing, looking outward.
I grasp the reins and hold the whip,
advancing and retreating with measure.
Joy departs, sorrow arrives,
a wistful and sudden realization.
I think of that respectful person,
with earnest longing and remembrance.
The sun and moon pass on,
the year approaches its end.
Alas, I, a young person,
am both dull and obstinate.
Is it not that my ambition is great,
but my talent is difficult to attain?
My life is not of metal or stone,
my body as light as morning dew.
How to know Sōng Qiáo,
and nourish the spirit in primal simplicity?
Wandering freely beyond the bounds,
to ascend my years and prosperity.

Chōng 鄭沖 and others deserve death.
We humbly observe that Your Excellency's auspicious mandate is clearly manifested,
and we secretly hear that Your Excellency firmly declines [the throne].
Chōng 鄭沖 and others are deeply attached [to the dynasty],
and we truly have a foolish heart,
believing that when sage kings established institutions,
a hundred generations followed the same customs.
Praising virtue and rewarding merit
has existed since ancient times.
In the past, Yī Yǐn 伊尹
was merely a dowry servant of the Yǒu Shēn 有莘 clan,
but by assisting Chéng Tāng 成湯 once,
he then bore the title of "Ā Héng" 阿衡;
the Duke of Zhōu 周公, taking advantage of an already established situation,
relying on a securely established enterprise,
gloriously resided in Qūfù 曲阜,
and wholly possessed Guī Méng 龜蒙;
Lǚ Shàng 呂尚,
a fisherman of Pán Creek 磻溪,
with a single morning's command,
was then enfeoffed at Yíngqiū 營丘.
Since then,
those whose merits were slight but rewards were great are too numerous to count,
Rán xiánzhé zhī shì yóu yǐ wéi měitán.
Moreover, since the time of the late Prime Minister,
generation after generation has possessed brilliant virtue,
assisting and supporting the House of Wèi,
in order to pacify the realm,
the court has lacked no proper governance,
and the people have had no cause for slander.
Previously, Your Excellency campaigned westward against Língzhōu,
approaching the northern desert,
west of Yúzhōng,
they submitted in awe at the mere sight of you.
The Qiāng and Róng tribes fled eastward,
turning their heads inwards (in submission);
eastward you punished rebellion and opposition,
the entire army achieved victory on its own,
capturing the generals of Hé Lǘ,
and beheading countless tens of thousands of crack troops,
your power extended to the South Sea,
and your name intimidated the Three Yuè;
peace and tranquility prevailed within the universe,
and oppression did not arise.
Therefore, foreign customs feared your might,
and the Eastern Yí offered dances (in tribute).
Therefore, the sage ruler has consulted the rites and regulations of the past,
opened the country, broadened the dwelling,
and made Taiyuan prominent.
Your Excellency should receive the imperial decree,
accept this great fortune,
and be worthy of both Heaven and humanity.
Your original achievements and great merits shine like the sun;
the blessings upon the country and its prosperity are as towering as mountains;
internally and externally, there is harmony and cooperation,
without any flaws or disobedience.
If you proceed with campaigns and conquests from this point forward,
you can then cross the river in court attire,
sweeping away Wú Kuài;
to the west, block the source of the river,
and offer sacrifices towards Mount Mín;
turning your spear and lowering your banners to command the world,
none far away will fail to submit,
and none near will fail to revere.
Let the virtue of great Wèi,
shine even brighter than that of Táng and Yú,
and let Your Excellency's great merits,
surpass those of Lord Huán and Duke Wén.
Then, overlooking Cāngzhōu, you can express gratitude to Zhī Bó,
and ascending Mount Jī, you can greet Xǔ Yóu.
Wouldn't that be magnificent!
Utterly just and fair,
who could be your neighbor!
Why bother with such humble declinations!
We, Chōng and others, do not understand the grand scheme,
and dare to present this to you.

Letter to the King Wén of Jìn Recommending Lú Bō
"Letter to the King Wén of Jìn Recommending Lú Bō"
I have heard that the key to flourishing civilization and successful governance
lies in obtaining the right people;
recruiting the extraordinary and selecting the exceptional
is the noble aspiration of sages and worthies.
Therefore, when the eight worthies returned to Zhōu,
the Zhōu dynasty prospered;
when Yú Shùn was promoted,
Yuán Kǎi and others all served with distinction.
I respectfully observe that Your Excellency, a duke and marquis,
embodies the refined essence of imperial spirit,
your nine virtues shine widely,
in response to the times, you act as an assistant,
discussing the Dao and spreading its influence,
opening the four gates [of opportunity],
He extends and receives worthy and wise men as wings,
to assist in grand prosperity.
Therefore, outstanding and talented men are willing to line up at the imperial gate,
to register their names and pledge their allegiance.
Those of true integrity and discernment flock to the grand administration;
truly, like the Dèng Lín 鄧林 forest, the Kūn Wú 昆吾 mountain, a place where soaring phoenixes roost.
Like the suspended black jade, the Hè Sì 和肆 marketplace,
a place where Chúi Jí 垂棘 gems gather.
I humbly observe that the Biejia of my humble prefecture,
Lú Bō 盧播 of the same commandery,
is thirty-two years old,
with the courtesy name Jǐngxuān 景宣.
From a young age, he possessed extraordinary talent and intelligence,
and as he grew older, he cherished noble and virtuous qualities.
He indulged in the Way and delighted in rituals,
relied on righteousness and depended on benevolence.
He diligently studied the ancient classics,
reaching the hall and perceiving the profound.
With keen insight, he discerned the principles of things,
and his mind understood the mysteries of the universe.
His integrity and steadfastness are sufficient to handle affairs,
his loyalty and reverence are sufficient to solemnize the court,
his clarity and decisiveness are sufficient to resolve doubts,
and his discretion and secrecy are sufficient to respond to exigencies.
He is not perplexed by troubles,
and becomes even brighter in times of urgency.
If he were to assist in governing and managing affairs,
Then (they are) instruments of governance;
entrusted with missions of envoys and tribute,
then (they are) talents for independent responses.
Immersed in books and records,
(they are) masters of literature;
skillful in composition and narration,
(they are) exemplars of good historians.
However, if learning is not for the sake of serving others,
and conduct does not seek advancement,
then one will long be submerged
and not attain high office.
Truly, he is an outstanding talent from the younger generation,
a useful instrument of the time,
and should receive official appointment
to harmonize the flavors of the tripod and balance the scales of state.
Confucius said:
"If someone is praised,
they must be tested."
The skills that he possesses,
are evident in his past achievements.
I dare not make false claims,
to invite criticism from the high authorities.

"Reply to Fúyì's Letter"
Jiè Bái writes:
Having received your message and read your intent,
I appreciate your well-intentioned written communication.
Now, the height of the nine heavens,
swift wings cannot reach its peak;
the depth of the four seas,
hidden scales cannot fathom its bottom;
how can one lacking even a feather's worth possibly comment on it?
Moreover, dark clouds have no fixed form,
and the *Yìnglóng* (responding dragon) does not adhere to a constant appearance:
sometimes crossing in the morning and receding in the evening,
emerging and vanishing alternately;
sometimes hiding in the mud and then flying to the sky,
descending at dawn and rising at dusk,
when extended, its form cannot be fully traced even across the eight cardinal directions,
and when contracted, no crevice is sufficient for it to be at ease;
this is something that even a blind man cannot perceive,
and a tiny insect cannot comprehend.
Therefore, that which is grand, cultivated, deep, and distant
cannot be fully explored through near effort;
and that which is spiritually transformative and divinely changing
cannot be observed by limited faculties.
Why must you, my friend, in your narrowness, seek the essence of such things with insistence?
Human abilities and circumstances cannot be uniform,
and preferences diverge.
*Luán* (mythical phoenix) and *fèng* (another mythical phoenix) soar across the Milky Way with dancing wings,
the turtledove and *yuān* (another type of bird) delight in wandering through the tangled forest;
the *chī* (hornless dragon) floats along the eight shores to bathe its scales,
Biē yú xínglǎo ér qún shì;
thus, they each employ their emotions, following their preferences to find pleasure.
To affirm this is to deny that,
how can they be considered the same?
When a person establishes a principle,
it is to cast a wide net to encompass the world,
how could they be confined by the constraints of a small net?
They are opening a mold to set an example for customs,
how can they spare time to degrade their essence to conform to superficial standards?
If good fortune is not in harmony,
and divine guidance is uncertain,
then they unleash their spirit and elevate their will,
transcending the world and soaring high,
elevating their essence beyond the realm of mystery,
expressing their sublime integrity beyond the nine heavens, riding the light, leaping and bounding,
surpassing hills, swift and elusive,
leisurely aligning with the transformations of the Dao,
carefree, flowing alongside the sun and moon,
intertwining their reputation with the void, becoming one with change,
reaching divine spirits, becoming equal in transformation,
ascending beyond the highest,
descending below the lowest,
residing in a place without rooms,
emerging from a place without doors,
unifying the going and staying of all things,
following the waxing and waning of the six energies,
encompassing the mysterious net within the Great Ultimate (Tàijí),
Embracing the Heavens within the vast expanse,
Floating dust cannot raise its waves,
Flying motes cannot tarnish its purity,
Merely lodging the physical form within this realm,
How can its spirit be perceived?
Though no pursuit is unheard of,
No account is unmentioned,
That understanding has limitations
is not surprising.
Observe the conduct of gentlemen:
Desiring to display the gold that could topple cities,
Seeking to sell it for a hundred coins;
Manufacturing rituals befitting Heaven,
Imitating the regulations for a mere inch;
Toiling the royal body in service to things,
Guarding filth and stench until the end;
Sinking in the dampness of an ox's footprint,
Resenting the rootlessness of the Milky Way;
Their vulgarity is shameful,
Their endeavors are pitiable.
Clearly knowing that plans are far beyond reach,
Truly believing in the vast and profound Great Way,
Yet confining their steps to the common crossroads,
Uselessly contemplating the distant, causing themselves sorrow.
Like a continuous rash, confused and muddled,
Forcibly explaining, though little is understood.

"Comprehensive Discussion on the Book of Changes"
Ruǎn Zǐ said:
What is the Book of Changes?
It is the ancient profound truth,
The changing classic of the past.
When Páo Xī Shì lived during the end of a cycle of heaven and earth,
He witnessed people and things in a state of exhaustion,
Useful things no longer existed,
Laws and institutions were simple and obscure,
The virtue of spiritual enlightenment was not attained,
And the emotions of all ages were not alike;
Therefore, he began to create the eight trigrams.
He extended and expanded them,
Lengthened them by association with similar things,
Divided Yin and Yang,
Arranged the firm and the yielding,
Accumulated mountains and marshes,
Connected water and fire,
Mixed them into one,
Transformed them to make them comprehensible,
Finally, the hexagram *Wèi Jì* (未濟, Not Yet Crossing)
, the sixty-four hexagrams are completed, yet not exhausted.
Therefore, Heaven and Earth are symbolized, and the myriad things take shape;
good fortune and misfortune are made manifest, and regret and disgrace arise;
the use of affairs has a purpose,
and changes have an accomplishment.
To face south and listen to judgments,
turn towards clarity and govern;
to knot cords and make nets and traps,
to bring about the goods of midday markets,
to cultivate the benefit of plows and hoes to teach,
the whole world is able to obtain its proper place.
*Huángdì* (黃帝), *Yáo* (堯), and *Shùn* (舜) responded to the times and attended to their duties,
each having their own choices;
exhausting the spirits and understanding transformation,
they narrated the order of Heaven.
*Páo Xī* shì (庖犧氏) spread and elaborated the changes of the sixty-four hexagrams;
later sages observed and followed them,
symbolizing and using them.
The classics of *Yǔ* (禹) and *Tāng* (湯) all existed,
but the writings of high antiquity do not survive;
until *Wén Wáng* (文王),
therefore he attached his explanations,
thereupon the *Guī Zàng* (歸藏) tradition faded and the *Zhōu* (周) classics flourished.
Above and below are not constant,
the firm and the yielding interchange;
it cannot be made into a fixed rule,
Only change is suitable,
therefore it is called "Yì" (易, Change).
The book called Yì,
is based on Heaven and Earth,
follows Yin and Yang,
infers flourishing and decline,
originates from the obscure and subtle and progresses to the clear and evident.
Therefore, the first line of Qián (乾) "Qián Lóng Wù Yòng (潛龍勿用, Hidden Dragon, Do Not Use)",
speaks of the virtue of the great person being hidden and not yet manifested,
concealed and not yet realized,
waiting for the time to rise,
following change to develop.
Heaven and Earth having been established,
Tún (屯) and Méng (蒙) begin to be produced,
Xū (需) is to wait for the time,
Sòng (訟) is to establish righteousness,
Shī (師) is to gather the masses,
Bǐ (比) is to pacify the people,
therefore, "the former kings established myriad states,
and cultivated close relations with the feudal lords",
to gather their hearts.
Tracing the origin and accumulating it,
nurturing and controlling it,
therefore, superiors and inferiors are in harmony and agreement,
"regulate and complete the Way of Heaven and Earth,
assist and support the suitability of Heaven and Earth to guide the people,"
following its principles.
After the former kings had passed away,
virtue and law deviated and changed,
superiors transgressed, and inferiors declined,
the ruler and ministers were unrestrained,
the firm and the yielding were not harmonious,
Heaven and Earth did not interact.
Therefore, gentlemen sought common ground with their own kind,
suppressing evil and promoting good,
in order to achieve their great ambitions.
They were humble and made it shine,
taking from the abundance and adding to the scarcity,
exalting the sage's goodness as their guiding principle.
Like thunder emerging from the earth,
then great men attained their positions,
and wise sages rose again.
Therefore, the former kings created music to offer sacrifices to the Supreme God,
illuminating their way to respond to Heaven's blessings.
Then all things submitted and obeyed,
following and serving them.
Sons followed their fathers,
and ministers obeyed their rulers.
Overseeing and unifying,
broadly observing the world,
therefore, the former kings used this to inspect the regions, observe the people, and establish education,
regulating them with standards.
Embracing and possessing it,
uniting and containing it,
therefore, the former kings used this to clarify punishments and regulate laws.
From above downwards,
the noble return to their humble origins.
Beauty becomes perfection, and prosperity reaches its limit.
The timing is extreme, and the sun reaches its zenith.
The former kings closed the borders;
merchants and travelers did not move.
The queen did not inspect the regions,
in order to pacify the people.
When the final era had already declined,
it was not obtained through scheming.
Responding to destiny and according with Heaven,
one acts without recklessness.
Therefore, the former kings greatly matched the times and nurtured all things,
bestowing benevolence and spreading blessings to establish their virtue.
All things return and follow,
like a flowing stream receiving.
Nurturing good and reversing evil,
accumulating benefits creates harm.
Excessive rigidity loses control.
Being accustomed to peril is the proper position.
When the superiors lose their way,
the inferiors lose their group.
Thereupon, great men continue the light of intelligence
and illuminate the four directions,
revealing their virtue.
Since the beginning of Qián Yuán (乾元),
impartiality and clarity have been implemented.
Prosperity and decline have their times;
rigidity and gentleness are not constant.
Sometimes gaining, sometimes losing,
one yin, one yang,
going out and coming in, auspiciousness and misfortune,
are discerned from darkness to clarity.
Stopping with civilization;
possess wings but do not fly.
Follow it and you will survive,
those who take from it will return,

sincerity without flattery or pleasing,

After the Confucians and Mohists,

They formed cliques and gathered into parties,

In the past, the powerful state of Dà Qí,

Thus, the trees in the mountains,

used allegories to broaden it,
borrowed from things to extend it,

Thereupon, these several gentlemen,

Now, the Nine Provinces have square and round (lands),
the Nine Fields have forms and features.
Regions have heights and depths,
things have their regulations:
open them, and they flow;
block them, and they are obstructed;
let them flow, and they move;
dam them, and they stop;
elevate them, and they become hills;
pollute them, and they become marshes;
winding and spreading,
encircled by great ravines.
Coming to the division into states and cities,
setting up representative objects,
the four seasons model their forms,
yin and yang harmonize their qi,
interconnecting and echoing,
having form and virtue,
clouds rise and thunder moves,
sometimes calling out, sometimes silent;
some find peace through them,
thus use them to anticipate delusion.
If we look at the gaps in the corners,
the paths in the remote wilderness,
the indistinct regions,
the capitals in the desolate fields;
strange, great, and cunningly bizarre,
one cannot fully depict them.
There are wandering scholars,
those with a refined spirit of expansive cultivation,
who brave the startling winds,
and tread upon the floating clouds;
the pure and impure both pass away,
good and ill fortune call to each other.
Therefore, Líng Lún 伶倫 wandered with the phoenix on the sunny side of Mount Kūnlún 崑崙,
Zōu Zǐ 鄒子 inhaled warmth on the shady side of the Millet Valley,

above, they wandered in the Xuán Pǔ 玄圃 garden,
below, they strolled in the Dèng Lín 鄧林 forest.
The phoenix sings on its own,
the soaring *luán* dances on its own,
the fine grains flourish,
not just our millet and rice.
In wretched and narrow places, there are fields for perverse arts,
ruins of deer and pigs,
not beautiful places of refinement,
but places where filth and accumulation gather.
To the west, heads are raised towards Ā Zhēn 阿甄,
and paths lead near Qī Pú 戚蒲,
mulberry trees are idle above the Pú River 濮,
a place of licentiousness and ruin.
The Three Jìn 三晉 are intertwined,
Zhèng 鄭 and Wèi 衛 are densely spread,
heroes and elites are continuous,
followers stay and live there.
Therefore, the strong and tyrannical are rampant in the households,
resentment and poison ferment in the corners of the bed,
they still plot evil at village drinking ceremonies,
how could it be that it would take a long time for it to erupt?
Its land is central,
the Liú and Wáng clans gather there.
High and dangerous, overlooking the city,
exhausted rivers surround the house.
The Shū clan marries within the family,
indeed living on its banks,
with their backs to the danger and facing the water,
filth and dirt are mostly private.
Therefore, in its villages and towns,
no one speaks of right or wrong,
suppressing emotions and wicked thoughts,
to cultivate their wealth.
Its farmland is desolate and barren,
planting crops is done at the wrong time,
fields are not opened,
thorns and brambles are not managed,
Liúhuáng yú táng,
spreading without end.
To the east, it faces the Three Qi states,
to the west, it borders Zou and Lu,
a long road of a thousand miles,
receiving these merchants;
using leisure as the standard,
with teachers and officials assisting,
arrogant servants and small towns,
are situated there.
Rivers and shortcuts,
Dòngtíng and Jīng Chǔ,
the remnants of their customs pass through,
this is the path and the house.
Following them, they continue the customs,
without principle, there is nothing to observe,
if not destroyed, there is no standard,
leading to ruin.
Therefore, their singing and harmonizing emphasizes power,
turning their backs on reason and facing treachery,
pursuing influence and chasing profit,
fearing only fault when acting according to deference.
Their dwellings are blocked and closed,
deep and dark without pattern,
leaning against mausoleums,
surrounded by winding rooms;
Therefore, dwelling in it causes the mind to become clouded,
speaking of it causes the will to grieve,
fear and confusion shift and change,
with nothing to awaken and cherish.
Outside it, there is the turbid river winding around its pond,
the clear Jì River washing against its fence.
To its north are connected ridges,
rising unevenly and ruggedly,
the mountains and hills towering,
clouds and lightning interacting,

desolate and vast plains.

rainwater forms pools,
deep forests and lush trees,
dense and uneven,
flocks of birds soar in the sky,
hundreds of beasts race about.
Even if the common people are not virtuous,
they still find contentment in the mountains and marshes.
The ancient wise men valued subtlety and refinement,
and loved the decorum of governance and teaching.
They treasured the profundity of the Mysterious Truth,
and delighted in the solitude of unknowing.
Alas for the scattered emotions of the common folk,
who ride the returning wind to raise their voices.
I gaze upon the wild and overgrown brambles,
and turn my head to the lush green of Dōngshān.
Sweet are the old sayings of the fields and villages,
so I utter new poems to comfort my feelings.
I trust that the harsh frost has not yet grown,
but how can the red wood flourish again?
"Běimén" grieves over deep sorrow,

Even the ceremonial feathers can feel the aspiration,

I suppress my frustration and think from afar,
the whirlwind gusts wildly, desiring to return.

raising this flock to compete in flight.

how can distant observation be pursued?

Rinse with the refreshing and pleasant jade-like liquid,

Black clouds rise and surround us,

lǜ mí yuǎn ér dù bī,
Wheels turning in narrow ditches,
As easily reached as the empty mulberry.
My words flow unrestrained,

I gather the announcements of Shū to take warning,

Confused and obscured, everything is disordered,

The principles are all mistaken and need to be re-established,

"Rhapsody on Mount Shǒuyáng"
In the autumn of the first year of Zhèngyuán,
I was still a court gentleman,
in the residence of the Grand General.
I went alone to the southern wall,
facing north towards Mount Shǒuyáng,
and composed the rhapsody:
At the end of this year,
The beginning of the ten-day period is heavy with yin.
CH0F02A8 The wind circles back, arriving in twists;
The rain spins around, soaking my delicate garment.
The cricket chirps in the eastern room,
The cuckoo cries in the western forest.
The time is nearing dusk and I have no companion,
My thoughts are sorrowful and affect my heart.
I shake the sandy clothes and go out the door,
My hat string is broken and cannot be found.
I pace back and forth, lost in distant thoughts,
I sigh deeply and hum softly.
I was about to groom myself and go out,

I am silent and alone, standing independently,
Clearly upright, relying on nothing.
I cherish the feeling of separation and isolation,
I detest the crowd of falseness shooting at the truth.
I believe in what is real and will not abandon it,
I would rather be lofty and prepare my own funeral.
For now, I lift my head and look around broadly,
I gaze at the peaks of Mount Shǒuyáng.
The trees are lush and leaning,
Confused and refreshing as they send their sound into the air.
Below, it is rugged and without shelter,
Above, it is clear and without support.
The phoenix flies past but does not gather here,
Owls hoot in groups and perch together.
Drifting afar and vanishing into the distance,
the two old men, impoverished, returned.
Truly confined and oppressed here,
how can we have leisure and dare to criticize?
The good grain is rejected and not preserved,
therefore they willingly die gathering ferns.
They turned their backs on Yīn and followed Chāng,
embracing danger and ruin without hesitation;
we advance but do not agree,
so what is this called but benevolence and righteousness?
Abandoning longevity and premature death to fate,
they compete to measure themselves by praise and blame.
Examining what the former records say,
what beautiful arguments are worthy of admiration?
If the Way is sought in the subtle,
why are you so extravagant and verbose?
Rather preserve the spirit with purity and emptiness,
why speak of it with such fervor?
"Ode to the Dove"
In the Jiāpíng year, I obtained two young doves,
which I regularly fed with millet and sorghum.
Later, they were eventually killed by a dog,
therefore I composed this ode.
Oh, the abundance of this auspicious year,
Hóng Zhào was dazed, as if awakening from ignorance.
There was a strange bird of appointed fate,
similar to the harmonious turtledove.
It flew amongst carved wood in a corner,
and nested upon a tall pine tree.
It inhaled clouds and mist for sustenance,
and roamed in the morning sun, keeping company.
After more than ten days, it produced offspring,
Commendably, seven sons of fine appearance.
They began to fold their wings and grow feathers,
encountering the rustling of the autumn wind.
Having toppled over with no rescue,
and shaken down with no assistance.
They roamed around Mount Huán,
and facing their old home, longed to enter;
raising mournful cries to send each other off,
grieving for their departure without return.
Finally, they fluttered about, scattered and displaced,
grieving over the trembling fear of the weak offspring.
On what to rely for nurture?
They relied on the kinship of brothers.
Turning their backs on the weeds to seek benevolence;
entrusting themselves to the quiet chamber of a gentleman,
relishing the fragrant cooked grains,
and finding peace in the doors and windows, free from disease.
With clean plumage, they intertwined necks,
discarding excessive splendor and brilliance,
She uses her beautiful and elegant figure to observe and adorn herself;
She loves her dignified appearance and maintains it consistently;
She lowers and raises her head leisurely and carefree;
Seeking affection and flattery today;
Why envy those who fly and soar?
Willing to repay kindness to the point of forgetting herself.
Encountering the violent rage of a mad dog,
Suffering intense harm to her small body;
Wanting to be utterly destroyed and annihilated,
She was abandoned and lost.
Alas, her humble and lowly state is lamentable,
How could one forget her even for a moment?
